name: block-destructive-commands
description: Best-effort, on parsed commands (echo ignored); one verdict table shared with rtk-dangerous-actions-blocker. Blocks recursive deletes of root, home, abs paths or .git; mv/chmod/chown -R of system dirs; dd to devices, mkfs; lockouts; force, delete, mirror pushes; history rewrites; switch --discard; IaC destroy; cloud deletes; DB drops. Asks: rm -rf off a safe list, one named kubectl delete, bare lease, stash drop, -auto-approve, drain, prunes, API deletes. Dry runs pass. Pre-push: no non-ff. [Best-effort in Devin by a PreToolUse hook shipped with the plugin's hooks.json (witnessed blocking on Devin CLI 3000.11.3 (local session), Windows, 2026-10-08). In the vendor's own words, plugin hooks are 'currently best effort and fail open -- if a hook fails to load or run, the session continues without it -- so don't rely on them for crucial guardrails yet', documented for local Devin sessions (the CLI and Devin Desktop) only. The hook command expands $DEVIN_PLUGIN_ROOT, an environment variable the vendor documents hook commands receive; whether that expansion happens inside a hooks.json command string is documented, not witnessed here. The hook needs git and a Python 3.11+ on PATH. Repo-wide git-hook and CI coverage still needs `chock sync`.]
